title: Robust experiment orchestration for model-variant evaluations and safety rollback
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Create a product-level A/B testing and canary framework for model versions that supports controlled exposure, shadow traffic experiments, sequential statistical checks, and automated rollback triggers tied to safety and quality SLOs.
background: Teams are increasingly onboarding new open and fine-tuned model variants to Redwood. Current rollouts are ad-hoc: simple traffic splits via routing rules with limited automated checks. We need a standardized framework that reduces manual guardrails, enables safer progressive exposure, and automates rollback when quality or safety regressions are detected.
goals: Provide a declarative experiment spec that engineers and PMs can use to declare canary/A-B/shadow experiments
Support dynamic exposure control (percent traffic, per-customer targeting, time windows)
Run continuous statistical tests with configurable error rates and sequential testing (to avoid peeking bias)
Integrate shadow traffic mode: mirror production traffic for validation without user impact
Enable automatic rollback policies based on customizable thresholds (latency, token error rates, safety hits, metric delta)
Instrument observability and experiment dashboards showing treatment/control comparisons and sample size progress
scope_included: Experiment spec schema (exposure, metrics, thresholds, duration)
Traffic routing primitives for percent and identity-based exposure
Shadow traffic pipeline with request sampling and KV-caching compatibility
Statistical engine: sequential tests (alpha spending / SPRT), uplift metrics, and false discovery correction
Auto-rollback actions wired into deployment controlplane (pause, revert traffic, send alert)
Dashboard view in Console summarizing experiments, sample stats, and rollback actions
scope_excluded: Full audit and compliance export for regulated customers (separate Private backlog)
Automated model retraining or parameter tuning as part of experiments
Routing across multiple cloud regions for the same experiment (MVP focuses on single-region experiments)
acceptance_criteria: Users can create an experiment via Console or API using the new spec and start/stop it
System enforces exposure caps and can target by customer IDs or routes
Shadow traffic pipeline ingests mirrored requests and stores request/response pairs for offline evaluation
Statistical engine computes treatment vs control metric deltas in near-real-time and surfaces confidence intervals
An experiment can be configured with an auto-rollback policy that executes when configured thresholds are exceeded
Console displays experiment status, sample sizes, key metrics, and recent rollback events
proposed_design: Users supply a YAML/JSON experiment spec with fields: baseline_model, candidate_model(s), exposure (percent / id-targeting), metrics (primary and safety metrics), statistical_policy (method, alpha, min_n), duration, and rollback_policy. The control plane orchestrates traffic routing; shadow traffic flows to an isolated store and the experiment engine evaluates metrics using streaming aggregation. The statistical engine supports alpha-spending and group-sequential methods to allow early stopping without inflation of type I error. Rollback actions call the deployment API to revert routing and create an incident ticket.
rollout_sequence: Draft experiment spec in Console or API
Start in shadow mode for 24-72h to validate stability and performance
Open to 0.5%-2% canary with sequential checks enabled
Progressively ramp exposure based on passing statistical gates and metric stability
Promote candidate to baseline or abort and auto-rollback if thresholds violated
stats_plan: Primary metric(s) defined per-experiment (e.g., reply latency p50, token-level safety hits, quality score). Default statistical method: alpha=0.05, sequential analysis via O'Brien-Fleming or alpha-spending. Provide options for Bayesian A/B for small-sample scenarios. Report uplift, p-values, and Bayesian posterior probabilities. Enforce minimum sample size before any promotion. Support multiple comparisons correction when K>1 candidates.
monitoring_and_rollback: Streaming monitors for latency regressions, exception rates, and safety classifier hits
Configurable thresholds (absolute or relative delta) that trigger soft actions (alerts, freeze ramp) or hard actions (immediate rollback)
Rollback choreography: revert traffic routing, mark model version as 'quarantined', surface incident link and changelog entry
Post-rollback diagnostics: collect recent request traces, sample mismatches, and compare cached KV hit rates
data_collection: Persist request context, prompt, response, latency, and model metadata for sampled requests
Retention policy configurable per-experiment (default 30 days for experiment artifacts)
Ensure PII filtering and redaction options are configurable to respect customer privacy
Expose export hooks (S3/Customer bucket) for offline evaluation and fairness audits
dependencies: ENG-7321: Traffic router extension for percent and identity targeting
ENG-7450: Shadow pipeline storage and redaction layer
ENG-7602: Streaming metrics aggregator and Console charts
ENG-7625: Deployment controlplane API for programmatic rollback
risks: Data privacy concerns in storing mirrored requests (mitigate via redaction and opt-outs)
Statistical misuse: misconfigured tests leading to false confidence (mitigate via sane defaults and warnings)
Operational complexity: rollback flapping if thresholds are too tight
Performance overhead from shadowing and additional metrics collection
tasks: Spec: define experiment schema and JSON/YAML grammar (PM + ENG)
API: create endpoints to create/start/stop/annotate experiments (ENG)
Router: implement identity-based routing and exposure caps (ENG)
Shadow: pipeline for mirrored requests with redaction (ENG)
Stats engine: implement sequential testing + dashboards (ENG + R&D)
Console: UI to author experiments and view live metrics (Design + ENG)
Docs: runbook for configuring metrics, interpreting tests, and rollback policy guidance (DX)
Security review: ensure redaction & KMS usage for experiment artifacts
